### `shoppingmall_products`

Represents a single product listing in the shopping mall catalog,
including base business, pricing, descriptive, and compliance-related
data. Major relationships include options (shoppingmall_product_options),
media (shoppingmall_product_media), associated tags (via
shoppingmall_product_tags), and snapshot versioning
(shoppingmall_product_snapshots). Main lifecycle: sellers create, update,
and deactivate products; admins may moderate or suspend. Historical state
is preserved via @link shoppingmall_product_snapshots.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_category_id`
  > Assigned category's [shoppingmall_categories.id](#shoppingmall_categories). Each product must
  > belong to one category.
- `shoppingmall_seller_id`
  > Product owner's seller account [shoppingmall_sellers.id](#shoppingmall_sellers).
  > References the seller responsible for this product.
- `sku`
  > Stock-keeping unit code as unique business identifier per product; unique
  > within the platform.
- `name`: Product name/title for catalog and search display.
- `description`
  > Long-form product description, supports rich text/markdown for customer
  > detail.
- `base_price`
  > Standard price for a single unit in the product's default configuration.
  > Excludes option upcharges, taxes, discounts.
- `currency`
  > ISO 4217 currency code representing product default currency (e.g.,
  > 'USD', 'EUR', 'KRW').
- `status`
  > Product status such as active, inactive, suspended, compliance_hold
  > (business/application-driven status, not an enum here for extensibility).
- `main_image_uri`: Primary display image URI for fast catalog rendering.
- `main_video_uri`
  > Primary display video URI for product feature/preview (e.g., for
  > video-rich listings).
- `sort_index`: Ordering index for product sort within its category or custom listings.
- `compliance_flag`
  > Whether this product is flagged for compliance/business review (true =
  > under review or hold).
- `created_at`: Product creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Product last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Product soft-deletion timestamp, if deleted; null if active.

### `shoppingmall_categories`

Defines structured product groupings for catalog navigation and AI
search. Supports hierarchical relationships for nested categories. Used
in [shoppingmall_products](#shoppingmall_products), and may reference templates ({@link
shoppingmall_category_templates}).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `parent_id`
  > Parent category self-reference {:link shoppingmall_categories.id}.
  > Enables hierarchical categories.
- `shoppingmall_category_template_id`
  > Applied template's [shoppingmall_category_templates.id](#shoppingmall_category_templates) for config,
  > validation, and layout.
- `code`
  > Machine-unique category code (used for lookups, templates, and
  > multi-language mapping).
- `name`: Human-readable category name for display and navigation.
- `depth`: Hierarchy level: 0=Root, 1=Level1, etc. For limiting depth/use.
- `sort_index`: Order within parent for catalog displays.
- `active`: Whether this category is currently enabled/visible.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete timestamp (logical removal).

### `shoppingmall_product_options`

Configurable options (e.g., color, size, bundle) associated with a
product. Each option defines a type, display name, and business logic for
variants. Related option values are in
shoppingmall_product_option_values.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_product_id`: Associated product's [shoppingmall_products.id](#shoppingmall_products).
- `option_type`
  > Business type (e.g., dropdown, radio, colorpicker, custom). String for
  > extensibility.
- `name`: Option display name (shown to users, e.g., Color, Size).
- `sort_index`: Sort order within all options for the product.
- `required`: Whether this option is required to complete a purchase.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Update timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_product_option_values`

Possible values under a given product option (e.g., Red/Blue for Color).
Defines business logic for SKUs, upcharges, and inventory splits. Used
for SKU configuration and stock.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_product_option_id`: Owning option's [shoppingmall_product_options.id](#shoppingmall_product_options).
- `value`: Value as shown to user and used for SKU construction (e.g., 'Red').
- `sort_index`: Ordering within the option (with lower index first).
- `price_override`
  > Optional price override/adjustment for this value; null if no adjustment
  > over base product price.
- `inventory_override`
  > Optional per-value inventory limit; null if subject to product-level
  > default.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Update timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_product_snapshots`

Historical record capturing a full product state (denormalized) for
versioning, compliance, and audit. Created at every business-relevant
product change. Used for rollback, legal evidence, and version-based
analytics. References main product in [shoppingmall_products.id](#shoppingmall_products).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_product_id`
  > Reference to the main product [shoppingmall_products.id](#shoppingmall_products) whose
  > state is captured.
- `sku`: Snapshot of the product's SKU at the time of the snapshot.
- `name`: Snapshot of the product's name at the time of the snapshot.
- `description`: Snapshot of the product description at the time of the snapshot.
- `base_price`: Snapshot of base price.
- `currency`: Snapshot of currency code.
- `status`: Snapshot of current status at the time of the snapshot.
- `main_image_uri`: Snapshot of display image URI.
- `main_video_uri`: Snapshot of display video URI.
- `shoppingmall_category_id`: Snapshot of the assigned category ID.
- `shoppingmall_seller_id`: Snapshot of the owning seller ID.
- `sort_index`: Snapshot of sort index.
- `compliance_flag`: Snapshot of compliance flag.
- `created_at`: Product creation timestamp as of the snapshot.
- `updated_at`: Product update timestamp as of the snapshot.
- `snapshot_created_at`: Timestamp this snapshot was created.

### `shoppingmall_category_templates`

Reusable templates for category logic (validation, presentation, or
default property sets). Used by categories as a base for config, layout,
or validation settings.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `code`: Template code uniquely identifying this template type.
- `name`: Human-friendly display name.
- `description`: Full template description or usage guide.
- `config_json`
  > Opaque configuration or schema as JSON string for extensibility and
  > future migration.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete timestamp (null if active).

### `shoppingmall_tags`

Atomic tag/label for product classification, filtering, and AI/search
optimization. Used as many-to-many via shoppingmall_product_tags. Unique
by code within a channel, name may duplicate. Related to products through
shoppingmall_product_tags.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_channel_id`
  > Owning channel for tag scope and disambiguation. {@link
  > shoppingmall_channels.id}.
- `code`: Machine-unique tag code, unique within a channel for fast lookup/search.
- `name`: Human-display name/label for UI and search.
- `type`: Business type/segment of tag (e.g., marketing, search, product, campaign).
- `sort_index`: Ordering within tag listings.
- `created_at`: Created timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Update timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_product_tags`

Junction table for many-to-many relationship between products and tags,
allowing one product to be associated with multiple tags.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_product_id`: Reference to product [shoppingmall_products.id](#shoppingmall_products).
- `shoppingmall_tag_id`: Reference to tag [shoppingmall_tags.id](#shoppingmall_tags).
- `created_at`: Timestamp tag was affixed to product.

### `shoppingmall_product_media`

Files, images, or videos attached to a product. Holds references to
[shoppingmall_products](#shoppingmall_products) and external file metadata/URIs. Separate
from main_image_uri in products for supporting galleries and asset
management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_product_id`: Owning product [shoppingmall_products.id](#shoppingmall_products).
- `media_type`: Business media type (e.g., image, video, document, 3d).
- `media_uri`: Resolvable URI for the media asset (uploaded or external).
- `alt_text`: Alternative text for accessibility and SEO.
- `sort_index`: Display ordering in gallery or product asset area.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_inventory_logs`

Immutable business audit and tracking record for inventory changes (stock
ins/outs, reservation, adjustment). Each log links the product, change
event, amounts, and actor/responsible. Used to analyze and audit
inventory and for compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_product_id`: Product whose inventory changed [shoppingmall_products.id](#shoppingmall_products).
- `actor_id`
  > Actor (seller/admin/system) responsible for this inventory event;
  > references shoppingmall_sellers, shoppingmall_admins, or system
  > integrators as appropriate.
- `change_type`
  > Type of inventory event (e.g., restock, reservation, checkout, cancel,
  > correction). Business-driven/extendable.
- `delta_quantity`: Change (positive/negative) in stock units.
- `inventory_before`: Units in stock before the event.
- `inventory_after`: Units in stock after the event.
- `context_json`
  > Opaque blob (JSON) for extensibility; holds details/context for event
  > (e.g., order ID, source, notes).
- `performed_at`: When inventory event actually occurred (business timestamp).
- `logged_at`: When the log was actually written (may differ for backfill, sync).

### `shoppingmall_seo_metadata`

SEO configuration/settings applied to a given product or category. Stores
meta fields for rendering/catalog/discovery and supports versioned
tracking through application-side logic. Can be attached to a product or
category. Used by AI/discovery/recommendation/search modules to influence
visibility, promotion, and targeting. Business uses: marketing, search
ranking, campaign optimization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_product_id`
  > Reference to product if applies to a product. {@link
  > shoppingmall_products.id}
- `shoppingmall_category_id`
  > Reference to category if applies to a category. {@link
  > shoppingmall_categories.id}
- `meta_title`: SEO meta title as used in HTML, SERP, SNS sharing.
- `meta_description`: Meta description field for SEO/search/social precision.
- `meta_keywords`: Comma-separated list of keywords/phrases for SEO context.
- `open_graph_json`
  > JSON object/struct (serialized) for open graph/social meta fields (e.g.,
  > og:image, og:type).
- `created_at`
  > Creation timestamp (business logic for update/version tracking handled
  > externally).
- `updated_at`: Last update (if focal fields change).

### `shoppingmall_carts`

Represents an active shopping cart session for a customer, supporting
multi-device and multi-channel commerce. Maintains association to the
owning customer, current session, and cart state. Each cart can contain
multiple items and is the anchor for snapshots and abandoned cart
tracking.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_customer_id`
  > Belonged customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers). Represents cart
  > owner.
- `shoppingmall_session_id`
  > Optional session's [shoppingmall_sessions.id](#shoppingmall_sessions). Represents
  > device/browser session owning the cart.
- `status`
  > Current cart status (e.g. 'active', 'checked_out', 'abandoned'). Business
  > logic driven.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when cart was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when cart was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp; null if active.

### `shoppingmall_cart_items`

Itemized list of products in each cart. References the containing cart,
product, and product option/variant, if any. Each row represents a single
product line in a cart with quantity and pricing snapshots for
auditability. No denormalized product data directly stored (refer via
snapshot if needed).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_cart_id`
  > Parent cart's [shoppingmall_carts.id](#shoppingmall_carts). Establishes cart to items
  > relationship.
- `shoppingmall_product_id`: Referenced product's [shoppingmall_products.id](#shoppingmall_products).
- `shoppingmall_product_option_id`
  > Optional product option's [shoppingmall_product_options.id](#shoppingmall_product_options). For
  > SKUs/variant selection.
- `shoppingmall_cart_snapshot_id`
  > Snapshot's [shoppingmall_cart_snapshots.id](#shoppingmall_cart_snapshots) at time of addition
  > (for precise state/historical audit).
- `quantity`: Quantity of this product in the cart line. Always > 0.
- `base_price`
  > Base price of product at time of addition. Copied from product snapshot
  > for audit; not recalculated.
- `applied_discount`: Discount applied per unit to this product line, if any.
- `final_price`
  > Final per-unit price in cart (after discounts, coupons, etc.). Calculated
  > for auditing at cart time only.
- `added_at`: Timestamp when item was added to cart.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when cart item was last updated.
- `removed_at`: Soft delete timestamp; null if active.

### `shoppingmall_cart_snapshots`

Snapshot of cart state at a specific point (e.g., add to cart, checkout,
or abandonment). Used for audit, analytics, order evidence, and recovery.
Contains denormalized (copied) data from the cart, customer, items, and
products for complete historical context.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_cart_id`: Cart's [shoppingmall_carts.id](#shoppingmall_carts) at snapshot moment.
- `snapshot_type`: Snapshot trigger event ('add_item', 'checkout', 'abandon', etc.).
- `snapshot_data`
  > Serialized JSON/business data containing cart, items, prices, customer,
  > and contextual info.
- `created_at`: Timestamp at which the snapshot was created.

### `shoppingmall_abandoned_carts`

Tracks carts that were abandoned by customers before checkout. Used for
analytics, recovery, and marketing triggers. Linked to session, customer,
and original cart for lifecycle tracking.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_cart_id`: Abandoned cart's [shoppingmall_carts.id](#shoppingmall_carts).
- `shoppingmall_customer_id`: Owning customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers).
- `shoppingmall_session_id`: Session's [shoppingmall_sessions.id](#shoppingmall_sessions) where abandonment detected.
- `abandoned_at`: Timestamp the cart was marked as abandoned.
- `recovery_status`: Status of recovery attempts ('none', 'emailed', 'recovered', etc.).
- `recovered_at`: Timestamp of successful recovery (if any); else null.

### `shoppingmall_cart_channels`

Associates carts with channels for multi-channel shopping, analytics, and
cross-device/cart migration. Each record links a cart to a specific
channel, supporting platform analytics and personalized cross-channel
flows.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_cart_id`: Linked cart's [shoppingmall_carts.id](#shoppingmall_carts).
- `shoppingmall_channel_id`: Linked channel's [shoppingmall_channels.id](#shoppingmall_channels).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when association was created.

### `shoppingmall_orders`

Main order entity for the shoppingMall platform. Stores core order
information, customer/seller references, channel origins, parent-child
linkage (split orders), top-line financials (non-calculated),
address/delivery data, order status, and assignment to
compliance/evidence flows. Links to snapshots, sub-orders, order items,
payments, shipments, refunds, returns, disputes, and status logs. Full
audit and regulatory preservation. Referenced by sub-orders, payments,
status logs, evidence, etc.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_customer_id`: Belonged customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers).
- `shoppingmall_seller_id`: Primary seller's [shoppingmall_sellers.id](#shoppingmall_sellers).
- `shoppingmall_channel_id`: Placed sales channel [shoppingmall_channels.id](#shoppingmall_channels).
- `order_code`
  > Order code, unique within channel—business order token (e.g.,
  > ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNN).
- `parent_order_id`
  > Parent order for split (multi-seller) orders; null if this is the
  > root/master order.
- `total_amount`
  > Sum of order item (raw price x quantity), pre-discount, pre-fee
  > (non-calculated, actual at order submit).
- `total_discount_amount`: Sum of applied discounts (at commit); always ≤ total_amount.
- `total_shipping_fee`: Order-level shipping/fulfillment fee (if paid by buyer).
- `order_status`
  > Current order status snapshot (enum: pending, confirmed, shipped,
  > delivered, completed, cancelled, on_hold, disputed, returned, refunded).
- `order_source`: Order creation source/channel (web, mobile, api, partner, etc.).
- `order_placed_at`: Timestamp order was submitted by user.
- `shipping_address_json`
  > Snapshot of the chosen shipping address at time of order as JSON
  > serialized structure. Immutable per business audit.
- `recipient_name`
  > Recipient's name (as entered for this delivery, for audit even if
  > different from profile).
- `recipient_phone`: Recipient phone/contact at order time (non-keyed to user profile).
- `created_at`: Created timestamp for order record.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp for order record.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp, null unless order record deactivated.

### `shoppingmall_sub_orders`

Sub-order record for multi-seller/multi-fulfillment cases. Each relates
to a master order and a specific seller. Captures order status, amounts,
and shipment cross-references. Sub-orders enable correct fulfillment,
cancellation, and partial refund flows. Parent order snapshotting is
referenced, with auditing. Links to order_items, shipments, status logs.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_order_id`: Referenced master order's [shoppingmall_orders.id](#shoppingmall_orders).
- `shoppingmall_seller_id`: Assigned seller (for this sub-order) [shoppingmall_sellers.id](#shoppingmall_sellers).
- `sub_order_code`
  > Unique code per sub-order within parent order context (e.g.,
  > ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNN-S01).
- `status`
  > Sub-order status (pending, confirmed, shipped, delivered, completed,
  > cancelled, on_hold, disputed, returned, refunded).
- `total_amount`: Total (raw) amount for this sub-order, as committed.
- `total_discount_amount`: Total applied discount on sub-order.
- `total_shipping_fee`: Shipping/fulfillment fee on sub-order (if borne by buyer).
- `created_at`: Sub-order creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp, null if active.

### `shoppingmall_order_items`

Order line items. Each references product snapshot and sub-order.
Captures product option, quantity, unit/total price at order commit,
per-business and audit rules. Supports reference to product snapshot for
audit and recovery. Enables evidence linkage and refund/return
calculation per item. No denormalization of live product info, strict
snapshot architecture. Indexed by sub-order, product, and code.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_sub_order_id`: Related sub-order [shoppingmall_sub_orders.id](#shoppingmall_sub_orders).
- `shoppingmall_product_snapshot_id`
  > Snapshot of product at order-time for this item {@link
  > shoppingmall_product_snapshots.id}.
- `product_option_json`
  > Serialized product option/sku snapshot as JSON at time of order (for
  > audit, e.g., color, size).
- `product_code`: Human-facing product code at order time (for audit).
- `product_name`: Product display name at order time (snapshot, audit).
- `quantity`: Purchased quantity for this item.
- `unit_price`
  > Per-unit price at order commit (actual raw price, not calculated current
  > price).
- `total_price`: Extended price (=unit_price x quantity) at commit.
- `created_at`: Order item record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Order item record last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp; null unless removed.

### `shoppingmall_order_payments`

Tracks all payment attempts for orders (initial, retry, split, partial,
failed, completed). References order, payer, payment method, gateway,
amount, status, and evidence. Follows full payment evidence and
reconciliation audit requirements. Used for refund initiation and
compliance linkage. No calculated fields, payment status and method must
be business-audited.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_order_id`: Related order [shoppingmall_orders.id](#shoppingmall_orders).
- `shoppingmall_customer_id`: Paying customer reference [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers).
- `payment_code`: Unique business payment transaction code, for support/audit.
- `amount`: Payment amount for this transaction (snapshotted at payment submit).
- `currency`: 3-letter ISO currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW).
- `payment_method`
  > Payment method (card, bank_transfer, deposit, coupon, mileage, ewallet,
  > cod, etc.).
- `payment_gateway`
  > Payment gateway/provider/business system (e.g., stripe, paypal,
  > wirebarley, bank name, or internal).
- `payment_status`
  > Current payment status (pending, success, failed, cancelled, on_hold,
  > refunded, disputed).
- `paid_at`: Timestamp of payment submission/commit.
- `gateway_transaction_id`: Gateway/reference transaction id/result for reconciliation.
- `created_at`: Payment record created at timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Payment record last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete for payment record if rolled back/erased.

### `shoppingmall_order_shipments`

Shipment/fulfillment records per (sub-)order. Tracks logistics
carrier/service, tracking code, fulfillment status, ship/receive/return
timestamps, and delivery audit. Primary linkage is to sub-order; supports
multi-shipment and partial fulfillment. All critical operations and
evidence linked for compliance. Supports returns, disputes, and delivery
tracking/audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_sub_order_id`
  > Related sub-order to which shipment is attached {@link
  > shoppingmall_sub_orders.id}.
- `shipment_code`: Internal shipment/tracking code for business use.
- `carrier`: Logistics company or carrier reference (business-facing).
- `tracking_number`: Carrier-assigned tracking id/code.
- `fulfillment_status`
  > Shipment fulfillment status (pending, ready, in_transit, delivered,
  > returned, cancelled, failed, lost, on_hold).
- `shipped_at`: Timestamp parcel was handed off to carrier/logistics.
- `delivered_at`: Timestamp parcel was officially delivered/accepted.
- `returned_at`: Timestamp of return-to-sender or failed delivery (if returned).
- `delivery_address_json`: JSON serial of the delivery/shipping address used (immutable for audit).
- `received_by`
  > Name or contact of person who physically received parcel, as known at
  > delivery time.
- `created_at`: Created timestamp for shipment record.
- `updated_at`: Updated timestamp for shipment record.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete, if shipment voided/erased.

### `shoppingmall_order_status_logs`

Immutable audit trail of all order & sub-order status transitions, with
actor, status before/after, timestamp, channel/context, and linkage to
compliance evidence where needed. Enables full lifecycle reconstruction
for audit/compliance/dispute. Used by admins for root cause and SLA
monitoring. Status log is append-only, write-once. Channel context for
multi-channel orders is preserved. Links to orders, sub-orders, and
evidence snapshots.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_order_id`
  > Main order mapped to this status change log {@link
  > shoppingmall_orders.id}.
- `shoppingmall_sub_order_id`
  > Sub-order mapped to this status change log (if applicable) {@link
  > shoppingmall_sub_orders.id}.
- `shoppingmall_actor_id`
  > Actor account triggering status change (customer, seller, admin) {@link
  > shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id}.
- `action_channel`: Channel/platform where status change originated (web, mobile, api, admin).
- `status_before`: Status before change occurred.
- `status_after`: Status after change occurred.
- `transition_reason`: Business reason or code for status transition.
- `transition_memo`
  > Arbitrary business logic memo or note for this transition (internal/audit
  > only).
- `transition_at`: Timestamp at which status change took place.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for log record.

### `shoppingmall_order_snapshots`

Immutable full-order snapshots for audit and compliance. Captures the
complete state (all business fields) of orders at critical points
(creation, payment, fulfillment, refund, dispute, etc.) for
evidence/audit purposes. Enables historical restoration, regulatory
export, and state transition analysis. Snapshot data are denormalized
JSON blobs, not real-time editable. Linked to original order.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_order_id`: Order to which this snapshot belongs [shoppingmall_orders.id](#shoppingmall_orders).
- `snapshot_type`
  > Nature of snapshot event (created, paid, shipped, delivered, refunded,
  > disputed, etc.).
- `snapshot_data_json`: Serialized JSON of the full order+items+shipments state at snapshot time.
- `created_at`: Snapshot record creation timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_order_refunds`

Refund/return payment flows attached to an order and often a sub-order or
specific item. Tracks refund amount, payment association, reason, admin
handling, and full audit trail for regulatory/compliance. Linked to
original payment, refund evidence, and status transitions. Governance for
partial/complete refunds, audit recovery, and regulatory SLA compliance.
No calculated fields (all values snapped at refund event).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_order_id`: Parent order [shoppingmall_orders.id](#shoppingmall_orders).
- `shoppingmall_payment_id`
  > Original payment transaction related to refund {@link
  > shoppingmall_order_payments.id}.
- `refund_code`: Unique refund transaction code (business/audit ref).
- `refund_amount`: Refunded amount for this event as of the snapshot.
- `refund_status`
  > Current refund status (pending, success, failed, cancelled, on_hold,
  > disputed).
- `reason`: Reason provided for this refund, business/audit context.
- `requested_by_role`: Role requesting refund (customer, seller, admin).
- `processed_by_role`: Role processing/approving refund (admin, seller, system).
- `requested_at`: Timestamp refund was requested/submitted.
- `processed_at`: Timestamp processed/approved/denied/failed.
- `created_at`: Refund record creation timestamp (business audit).
- `updated_at`: Refund record last updated (audit trail/compliance).

### `shoppingmall_order_returns`

Return requests (prior to refund) attached to orders, sub-orders, and
items. Contains business logic for eligibility (date, condition), scope,
reason, and processing details. Linked to refund flows when approved.
Tracks processing/admin roles, evidence, and audit trail for regulatory.
Supports multi-item, partial, or complete returns per order. Each return
record is uniquely linked to order, items, and refund when approved.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_order_id`: Order containing the item(s) to return [shoppingmall_orders.id](#shoppingmall_orders).
- `shoppingmall_refund_id`
  > Refund record created if/when return is approved/paid {@link
  > shoppingmall_order_refunds.id}.
- `return_code`: Unique return request code for audit/business trace.
- `return_type`: Type: full or partial (itemized).
- `status`
  > Current status (pending, approved, rejected, cancelled, returned,
  > completed, failed, on_hold).
- `reason`: Customer/business reason for initiating return.
- `item_list_json`
  > JSON array of items and quantities to return (structured for itemized
  > returns).
- `requested_by_role`: Who initiated: customer, seller, or admin?
- `processed_by_role`: Approver/process role: admin, seller, system.
- `requested_at`: Return requested timestamp.
- `processed_at`: Return processing/approval/denial time.
- `created_at`: Return record creation time.
- `updated_at`: Last update to return record.

### `shoppingmall_disputes`

Formal disputes raised regarding order, payment, refund, or delivery.
Contains status, subject type, related objects, open/close details,
reason, and evidentiary snapshot. Enables compliance and legal handling;
supports foreign linkages to refund, return, shipment, and order
evidence. Used for regulatory/consumer issues and audit compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_order_id`: Main (root) order subject of dispute [shoppingmall_orders.id](#shoppingmall_orders).
- `shoppingmall_refund_id`: Refund in dispute if applicable [shoppingmall_order_refunds.id](#shoppingmall_order_refunds).
- `shoppingmall_return_id`: Return in dispute if applicable [shoppingmall_order_returns.id](#shoppingmall_order_returns).
- `shoppingmall_shipment_id`
  > Shipment/fulfillment in dispute if applicable {@link
  > shoppingmall_order_shipments.id}.
- `dispute_code`: Globally unique dispute identifier for audit.
- `dispute_type`: Nature of dispute (order, refund, return, shipment, product, etc.).
- `status`
  > Status (pending, open, resolved, rejected, cancelled, escalated, on_hold,
  > closed).
- `opened_by_role`: Role that initiated dispute (customer, seller, admin).
- `opened_at`: Dispute case opened time.
- `closed_by_role`: Role closing the dispute (admin, seller, customer, system).
- `closed_at`: Case closed time (if resolved or rejected).
- `dispute_subject_json`
  > JSON snapshot of disputed object context (order, payment, refund,
  > delivery, product).
- `resolution_summary_json`
  > JSON narrative/structure of how dispute was settled (compliance/legal
  > trace).
- `created_at`: Dispute record creation (audit).
- `updated_at`: Last update to dispute record.

### `shoppingmall_order_evidence`

Evidence and audit-trail linkage table for all order-related compliance
events (creation, update, refund, dispute, return, shipment). Records
event, type, business context, actor, and snapshot. Enables full
traceability for legal, SLA, or regulatory requirements. Supports
bulk/batch download for legal hold or regulatory export.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shoppingmall_order_id`: Order this evidence is bound to [shoppingmall_orders.id](#shoppingmall_orders).
- `shoppingmall_actor_id`
  > Actor (user, seller, admin) who created this evidence (links to
  > audit/compliance user profile) [shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id](#shoppingmall_actor_profiles).
- `evidence_type`
  > Nature/type: creation, payment_submit, payment_complete, shipment,
  > delivery, refund, return, dispute, cancellation, compliance, system, etc.
- `evidence_context_json`
  > Serialized JSON of the business context for evidence (order, payment,
  > reason, files, etc.).
- `created_at`: Evidence record creation time.

### `shoppingmall_coupon_templates`

Defines the master templates for coupons, including rules for benefit
calculation, eligibility, allowed stacking, redemption windows, and
associated metadata. This table structures business logic applicable to
batches of issued coupons and supports both platform (admin) and
seller-originated campaigns. Supports audit trails for retroactive policy
changes and analytics for benefit optimization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `created_by_admin_id`: Admin's [shoppingmall_admins.id](#shoppingmall_admins) who created this coupon template.
- `created_by_seller_id`
  > Seller's [shoppingmall_sellers.id](#shoppingmall_sellers) who created this coupon template
  > (nullable if admin-created).
- `type`
  > Type of coupon: one of fixed_amount, percentage, free_shipping, etc. Used
  > for determining benefit calculation logic.
- `name`: Business-facing name of the coupon template.
- `description`
  > Long-form business description for the template, explaining business
  > context, user eligibility, and restriction rules.
- `start_at`
  > Window start timestamp when coupons based on this template become valid
  > for redemption.
- `end_at`
  > Window end timestamp after which no more coupons from this template can
  > be issued or redeemed.
- `min_order_amount`
  > Business rule: minimum order amount required to enable coupon usage (if
  > applicable).
- `max_discount_amount`
  > Maximum discount amount allowed for this template, used to cap value in
  > percent-based or stackable offers.
- `issued_quantity`: Total number of coupons issued from this template.
- `allowed_uses_per_user`
  > Maximum number of times a single user can redeem coupons from this
  > template.
- `combinable`
  > Indicates whether coupons using this template can be stacked (combined)
  > with others in a single order.
- `active`
  > Shows if the template is currently active (no subsequent issuance if
  > false).
- `metadata_json`
  > Business extensibility field for extra metadata (JSON encoded for
  > flexible business logic).
- `created_at`: Template creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last template modification timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion timestamp, null until business removal required.

### `shoppingmall_coupons`

Represents individual coupons issued to the platform or sellers,
inheriting rules from the template table. Tracks coupon code, assignment,
status, and base eligibility parameters (e.g., target user, valid window,
original value).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `coupon_template_id`: Originating template's [shoppingmall_coupon_templates.id](#shoppingmall_coupon_templates).
- `coupon_code`
  > Globally unique code or identifier for the coupon (redeemable by user at
  > checkout).
- `assigned_to_customer_id`
  > Customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers) this coupon is assigned to
  > (nullable until claimed or issued).
- `issued_to_seller_id`
  > Seller's [shoppingmall_sellers.id](#shoppingmall_sellers) if coupon is restricted to a
  > specific seller (nullable if platform-wide).
- `issued_at`: Timestamp when this coupon was issued to user or made available for claim.
- `expires_at`
  > Business expiry date for this coupon (cannot be redeemed after this point
  > even if template valid).
- `redeemed`: State flag indicating if coupon has been redeemed at least once.
- `locked`
  > If true, this coupon is temporarily or permanently locked by
  > business/validation rules (e.g., fraud, dispute, compliance).
- `metadata_json`
  > Business extensibility: optional JSON for assigning additional metadata,
  > campaign info, or error traces.
- `created_at`: Coupon creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Coupon last updated timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion timestamp, null unless business removal required.

### `shoppingmall_coupon_issuances`

Tracks every coupon issued from a template, identifying the actor (admin
or seller), time, method (bulk, direct, user-claim), and context. This
model is used for benefit auditing and campaign analytics.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `coupon_id`: Issued coupon's [shoppingmall_coupons.id](#shoppingmall_coupons).
- `issued_by_admin_id`
  > Admin's [shoppingmall_admins.id](#shoppingmall_admins) who issued the coupon (if
  > admin-driven).
- `issued_by_seller_id`
  > Seller's [shoppingmall_sellers.id](#shoppingmall_sellers) if coupon issued by seller, null
  > if platform-only.
- `issue_method`
  > Describes business method of issuance: e.g., 'direct_assign',
  > 'bulk_event', 'self_claimed', etc.
- `context_json`
  > Additional business context of issuance (trigger event, segmentation,
  > batch info, etc.), JSON encoded.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this issuance was created.

### `shoppingmall_coupon_redemptions`

Records each redemption event for coupons. Links coupon, redeemer
(customer), redemption context, result, and timestamps. Used for
enforcement of benefit usage rules and benefit dispute evidence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `coupon_id`: Coupon's [shoppingmall_coupons.id](#shoppingmall_coupons) being redeemed.
- `redeemed_by_customer_id`: Customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers) who redeemed the coupon.
- `order_id`
  > Order's [shoppingmall_orders.id](#shoppingmall_orders) where coupon was used (if known at
  > time of redemption).
- `benefit_amount`
  > Amount of benefit redeemed (currency value for discount or actual value
  > of benefit).
- `redemption_result`
  > Outcome/result status of redemption: e.g., 'success', 'failed_minimum',
  > 'expired', 'disputed'.
- `redemption_context_json`
  > Business context for redemption (e.g., reasoning, cart snapshot), JSON
  > encoded.
- `redeemed_at`: Redemption event timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_mileage_ledger`

Records all mileage (loyalty point) accruals and deductions for
users—including initial award, promotional boosters, redemptions,
expirations, reversals, and admin/seller/manual adjustments. Supports
full auditability by point origin, value, event, and status.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers) who owns this ledger record.
- `admin_id`
  > Admin's [shoppingmall_admins.id](#shoppingmall_admins) who performed manual mileage
  > adjustment (nullable if system-driven).
- `seller_id`
  > Seller's [shoppingmall_sellers.id](#shoppingmall_sellers) who performed mileage adjustment
  > (nullable if not seller-driven event).
- `event_type`
  > Describes the business event: e.g.,
  > 'order_award','coupon_bonus','redemption','expiration','manual_adjustment'.
- `mileage_delta`
  > Number of points accrued (+) or deducted (-) from user's balance in this
  > event.
- `related_order_id`
  > Order's [shoppingmall_orders.id](#shoppingmall_orders) linked to this mileage event (null
  > if not order-related).
- `notes`
  > Free-form admin or business-facing notes, e.g., explanation for manual
  > adjustment or error context.
- `created_at`: Mileage event creation timestamp.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when mileage expires (null if not expired or not per-point
  > expiry model).

### `shoppingmall_deposit_ledger`

Tracks all deposit balance-related activities for a user, including
top-ups, deductions for orders, refunds, expiration, and provider-based
adjustments. Supports full business/audit trace from original event to
each impact on the user's account.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`
  > Customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers) whose deposit balance is
  > impacted.
- `admin_id`
  > Admin's [shoppingmall_admins.id](#shoppingmall_admins) performing deposit action (if not
  > system-driven).
- `event_type`
  > Describes the deposit business event: e.g.,
  > 'topup','order_payment','refund', 'expiration','manual_adjustment'.
- `amount_delta`: Deposited (+) or deducted (-) amount of funds (platform currency units).
- `related_order_id`
  > Order's [shoppingmall_orders.id](#shoppingmall_orders) if event is related to an order
  > transaction.
- `provider`
  > Payment provider identifier (e.g.,
  > 'credit_card','bank_transfer','voucher', etc.).
- `notes`: Admin or system notes for business/audit/exception context.
- `created_at`: Deposit event creation timestamp.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when deposit expires (if per-transaction expiration/policy
  > applies).

### `shoppingmall_benefit_snapshots`

Historical business snapshots of user benefit entitlements at the time of
issuance, redemption, or adjustment—used for compliance, disputes, legal
evidence, and retroactive benefit restoration. Stores point-in-time,
immutable business records for every coupon, mileage, or deposit event.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`
  > Customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers) whose benefit entitlement is
  > snapshotted.
- `benefit_type`: Type of benefit at snapshot: 'coupon', 'mileage', or 'deposit'.
- `source_id`
  > ID of the source entity (coupon_id, mileage_ledger_id, or
  > deposit_ledger_id as applicable).
- `snapshot_json`
  > Full snapshot of business state and entitlements at point-in-time (JSON
  > encoded).
- `event_type`
  > Triggering event: 'issuance', 'redemption', 'adjustment', 'expiration',
  > 'rollback', etc.
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_benefit_audit`

Immutable, tamper-evident audit log for all benefit (coupon, mileage,
deposit) events, including issuance, redemption, expiration, failure, and
business corrections. Critical for compliance, business rule enforcement,
and regulatory retrieval.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `source_id`: Source entity for audit (may refer to coupon, mileage, or deposit entry).
- `customer_id`
  > Customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers) whose benefit action is
  > being audited.
- `benefit_type`: Type of benefit impacted: 'coupon', 'mileage', or 'deposit'.
- `event_type`
  > Business event: 'issuance',
  > 'redemption','expiration','manual_correction','auto_expire', 'dispute',
  > etc.
- `event_context_json`: Business context or metadata for this event (JSON encoded).
- `created_at`: Audit event creation timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_coupon_errors`

Represents business, eligibility, validation, and redemption errors
related to coupon usage. Used to improve user experience, root cause
analysis, and business policy refinement. Supports both user-facing and
internal error reporting.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `coupon_id`: Coupon's [shoppingmall_coupons.id](#shoppingmall_coupons) related to this error event.
- `customer_id`
  > Customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers) affected by this error
  > occurrence.
- `error_code`
  > Application/business error code (e.g., 'COUPON_EXPIRED',
  > 'COUPON_INELIGIBLE').
- `error_message`
  > User-facing or system error message explaining cause and suggested
  > remediation.
- `business_context_json`: Optional serialized business context for error (JSON encoded).
- `created_at`: Error event occurrence timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_articles`

Business articles and editorial posts for the shoppingMall community and
platform. Managed by admins or authorized sellers, these support platform
news, guides, major updates, editorial content, and feature rollouts.
Audience is customers and sellers. Threaded comments, content snapshots,
and compliance audit tracked via related models. Subject to moderation,
reporting, and analytics through related entities.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `created_by_id`: Actor's [shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id](#shoppingmall_actor_profiles) who created the article.
- `title`: Article title. Shown in listings, SEO, and notifications.
- `body`: Full published content of the article. May include rich formatting.
- `summary`
  > Short summary for preview or search result snippets. Typically 100-300
  > chars.
- `cover_image_uri`
  > Cover image for this article, used in lists and previews. Must be a valid
  > image URI or file reference.
- `pinned`
  > Whether this article is currently pinned at the top of listing pages or
  > dashboards. Admin only.
- `published_at`: Datetime article was made public. Null if draft or pending.
- `created_at`: Datetime of initial article creation. Immutable, for evidence and audit.
- `updated_at`: Datetime of most recent edit. For audit and dashboard display.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion flag. Set when logically deleted, retained for compliance
  > and evidence.

### `shoppingmall_comments`

Threaded comments for UGC articles, inquiries, reviews, or bulletins.
Supports nested replies via parent-child hierarchy. Moderation,
reporting, evidence, and analytics handled by related models. Each
comment links to content target, owning actor, and may be soft-deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `parent_id`
  > Self-referential. The parent comment's [shoppingmall_comments.id](#shoppingmall_comments),
  > for nested comment threads.
- `thread_id`
  > The root thread's [shoppingmall_thread_statistics.id](#shoppingmall_thread_statistics) this comment
  > belongs to, grouping all comments for a single content object.
- `author_id`: Actor's [shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id](#shoppingmall_actor_profiles) who posted the comment.
- `body`: Comment message content. Plain text or optionally formatted by policy.
- `edited`
  > Whether this comment has been edited after initial submission. Used for
  > audit and display.
- `created_at`: Datetime when comment was first created. Immutable.
- `updated_at`: Datetime when comment was last edited. Changes if edited=true.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion field. Null unless deleted.

### `shoppingmall_inquiries`

Product, service, or bulletin Q&A inquiries initiated by authenticated
users. Each inquiry is linked to a product, article, or bulletin (via
foreign key or thread linkage), supports status tracking, moderation, and
evidence/audit via snapshots. Answers are managed in separate table.
Reporting, flagging, and compliance handled via related entities.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `thread_id`
  > The root thread's [shoppingmall_thread_statistics.id](#shoppingmall_thread_statistics) for this
  > inquiry (groups all posts: Q&A, comments, stats, etc.).
- `customer_id`: Inquiry by customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers).
- `target_product_id`: Target product's [shoppingmall_products.id](#shoppingmall_products) (if product inquiry).
- `target_article_id`: Target article's [shoppingmall_articles.id](#shoppingmall_articles) (if article inquiry).
- `target_bulletin_id`: Target bulletin's [shoppingmall_bulletins.id](#shoppingmall_bulletins) (if bulletin inquiry).
- `question`
  > Full inquiry question submitted by user. Subject to profanity check,
  > validation. Min 10, max 1000 characters.
- `status`
  > Business status code of inquiry: pending, answered, closed, or escalated,
  > per business rules.
- `created_at`: Datetime of inquiry submission. Immutable, for evidence and search.
- `updated_at`: Datetime of most recent inquiry update or status change.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion. Set when logically removed for compliance, evidence, or
  > policy.

### `shoppingmall_inquiry_answers`

Official answers (from seller or admin) to inquiries. Answers are 1:1
with inquiries but may support edits and history (tracked by snapshots).
Clearly associated to responding actor, with audit and compliance
requirements. Used for business/role escalation workflows.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `inquiry_id`: Target inquiry's [shoppingmall_inquiries.id](#shoppingmall_inquiries) being answered.
- `responder_id`
  > Actor's [shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id](#shoppingmall_actor_profiles) who responded. Must be
  > seller or admin.
- `body`
  > Answer message content. May support rich text or formatting depending on
  > business logic.
- `edited`
  > Whether this answer has been edited after initial submission. Used for
  > audit purposes.
- `created_at`: Datetime when answer was first created. Immutable.
- `updated_at`: Datetime when answer was last edited. Changes if edited=true.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion field. Set when answer removed logically, retained for
  > audit.

### `shoppingmall_reviews`

Product, service, or seller reviews entered by customers after
purchase/fulfillment. Each review links to a thread, the reviewed entity
(product or seller), and the submitting customer. Supported features:
star rating, text content, optional media, moderation, reporting, and
analytics. Review edits and compliance evidence retained via snapshots.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `thread_id`
  > The root thread's [shoppingmall_thread_statistics.id](#shoppingmall_thread_statistics) for this
  > review and all replies/posts.
- `customer_id`: Authoring customer's [shoppingmall_customers.id](#shoppingmall_customers).
- `target_product_id`
  > Reviewed product's [shoppingmall_products.id](#shoppingmall_products). Null if not a
  > product review.
- `target_seller_id`
  > Reviewed seller's [shoppingmall_sellers.id](#shoppingmall_sellers). Null if not seller
  > review.
- `rating`
  > Business review score. 1 to 5 stars, inclusive. Enforced by validation
  > logic.
- `title`: Short review title, used in lists or search. Optional.
- `body`
  > Review content body. Min 10, max 2000 characters. Must pass validation
  > and moderation.
- `verified_purchase`
  > Indicates if review is from a verified purchase/order (for business trust
  > badge display).
- `created_at`: Datetime of review submission. Immutable, for time-based sort or evidence.
- `updated_at`: Datetime of most recent review update (body, title, etc).
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp, if removed logically for policy/compliance.

### `shoppingmall_review_replies`

Authoritative replies to reviews from sellers or admins. One reply per
review. Replies support moderation, edits, evidence/audit, and can be
flagged for abuse. Each is associated to a review and responding actor
role.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `review_id`: Target review's [shoppingmall_reviews.id](#shoppingmall_reviews) being replied to.
- `responder_id`
  > Actor's [shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id](#shoppingmall_actor_profiles) replying to the review.
  > Usually a seller or admin.
- `body`: Reply message content, including moderation notes or acknowledgments.
- `edited`
  > Whether this reply has been edited after submission. Required for
  > evidence and audit.
- `created_at`: Creation datetime of review reply. Immutable.
- `updated_at`: Datetime of most recent edit to reply.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion flag. Set when reply logically deleted (policy/compliance).

### `shoppingmall_bulletins`

Bulletin board posts and platform-wide announcements. Created mainly by
admins but can be posted by designated sellers for community marketing,
legal, or major campaign notices. Supports pinning, expiration, and
visibility logic. Audit and content evidence preserved for compliance
uses. Comments and reporting supported via related models.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `author_id`
  > Actor's [shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id](#shoppingmall_actor_profiles) who posted the bulletin
  > (admin or seller).
- `title`: Bulletin headline or title. Used for listings, links, and notifications.
- `body`: Bulletin message content. Can include formatting, images, or legal text.
- `pinned`: If the bulletin is currently pinned at the top of listings. Admin only.
- `visible_to`
  > Visibility policy: all, customers, sellers, or admin-only. Used to
  > restrict who sees a post.
- `expire_at`: Optional expiration; bulletin hidden after this date for users.
- `created_at`: Datetime of creation. Immutable, for evidence and compliance.
- `updated_at`: Datetime of last edit or update. Tracked for moderation/audit.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion. Set when logically removed, but still retained for
  > compliance period.

### `shoppingmall_reported_content`

Business-level content abuse or violation reports filed by users or
detected by automated systems. Supports multi-type (comment, review,
bulletin, article, etc.) targeting, links to reporting actor, management
status, and audit evidence. Used for moderation, compliance, and
regulatory escalation when required.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `reported_by_id`
  > Actor's [shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id](#shoppingmall_actor_profiles) who filed the report
  > (customer, seller, or admin).
- `target_comment_id`
  > Reported comment's [shoppingmall_comments.id](#shoppingmall_comments), if report is for a
  > comment.
- `target_article_id`
  > Reported article's [shoppingmall_articles.id](#shoppingmall_articles), if report is for
  > article.
- `target_inquiry_id`: Reported inquiry's [shoppingmall_inquiries.id](#shoppingmall_inquiries), if applicable.
- `target_review_id`: Reported review's [shoppingmall_reviews.id](#shoppingmall_reviews), if applicable.
- `target_bulletin_id`: Reported bulletins's [shoppingmall_bulletins.id](#shoppingmall_bulletins), if applicable.
- `reason_code`
  > Machine- or user-generated reason code: spam, abuse, fraud, policy,
  > legal, etc. Used for escalation path and analytics.
- `narrative`
  > Additional free-text context or details from the reporter. May be null
  > for automated detection.
- `status`
  > Status of the report: open, reviewed, actioned, closed, escalated, etc.
  > Tracked for compliance evidence.
- `created_at`
  > Date/time report was filed or auto-generated. Immutable, for business
  > logic and SLA audit.
- `updated_at`
  > Date/time of last moderation action or status update. Changes as review
  > proceeds.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion for compliance evidence, set when logically removed.

### `shoppingmall_content_flags`

Internal or user-triggered moderation flags on content. Used to mark
possible abuse, offensive, or out-of-policy cases pending review.
Actioned by admins, linked to flagged actor, content, and
compliance/audit evidence. Subject to auto-escalation on threshold or
legal/AI detection.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `flagged_by_id`
  > Actor's [shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id](#shoppingmall_actor_profiles) who flagged the content
  > (or system/AI).
- `target_comment_id`: Flagged comment's [shoppingmall_comments.id](#shoppingmall_comments), if content is comment.
- `target_article_id`: Flagged article's [shoppingmall_articles.id](#shoppingmall_articles), if content is article.
- `target_inquiry_id`
  > Flagged inquiry's [shoppingmall_inquiries.id](#shoppingmall_inquiries), if content is
  > inquiry.
- `target_review_id`: Flagged review's [shoppingmall_reviews.id](#shoppingmall_reviews), if content is review.
- `target_bulletin_id`
  > Flagged bulletins's [shoppingmall_bulletins.id](#shoppingmall_bulletins), if content is
  > bulletin.
- `flag_type`
  > Flag category code: abuse, spam, copyright, prohibited, etc. Used for
  > business rule/action routing.
- `note`
  > Free-text note from actor, may include context or evidence pointer. May
  > be null for automated/AI flags.
- `status`: Status of moderation: pending, reviewed, actioned, dismissed.
- `created_at`
  > When flagged record was created (user or automated). Immutable for
  > evidence and audit.
- `updated_at`: Datetime last updated, typically by moderator or system.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion field for legal compliance/audit retention.

### `shoppingmall_content_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots of content items (comments, reviews, inquiries,
articles, bulletins, etc.) for compliance, audit, dispute resolution, or
history navigation. Each links to original content, content type, and
change context. Tied to thread and actor. Only created by business events
(change, deletion, dispute, etc.).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `thread_id`
  > Content thread's [shoppingmall_thread_statistics.id](#shoppingmall_thread_statistics) for full audit
  > trail linkage.
- `actor_id`
  > Actor's [shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id](#shoppingmall_actor_profiles) who triggered the snapshot
  > (admin, seller, customer, or system).
- `content_type`
  > Content type: comment, review, inquiry, article, bulletin, etc. Used to
  > interpret content_id and reconstruction.
- `content_id`
  > UUID of the content object being snapshotted. Must correspond to correct
  > type/target table.
- `snapshot_body`
  > Full serialized snapshot of content at the time of event. Content
  > structure depends on type.
- `change_event`
  > Business code for what caused snapshot (create, edit, delete, moderation,
  > dispute, etc.).
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation datetime. Immutable evidence timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_thread_statistics`

Materialized/statistics entity for each thread of user/community content
(article, review thread, inquiry thread, bulletin thread, etc.). Stores
denormalized statistics and trust signals (post count, like count, abuse
count, moderation history) for performance analytics and UI display.
Serves as anchor/root for comments and thread association. Managed as
non-materialized business table for performance and audit requirements,
not for direct content display.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `thread_type`
  > Thread context type: article, review, inquiry, bulletin, etc. Used for
  > analytics and UGC linkage.
- `target_id`
  > UUID of top-level content entity this thread is for (article, review,
  > inquiry, etc).
- `post_count`
  > Denormalized count of posts/comments/content in this thread. Used for
  > analytics and query performance.
- `like_count`
  > Like/upvote count associated with content in this thread. Used for
  > trust/trending UI.
- `abuse_report_count`
  > Count of abuse/report/flag submissions related to thread content. Tracked
  > for moderation escalation and analytics.
- `last_posted_at`: Datetime when last post was made to this thread (audit, recency ranking).
- `created_at`: Thread statistics row creation datetime.
- `updated_at`: Datetime statistics row was last updated.

### `shoppingmall_favorites`

Stores summary record of all favorites for a user, with role,
entity-type, current status, and logical deletion. References user
(customer, seller), relates to specific domains such as products,
inquiries, or addresses. Central linking table for favorites logic. Used
for managing favorites lifecycle, restoration, deactivation, and
engagement analytics.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `actor_profile_id`
  > Actor performing the favoriting action. References the user's {@link
  > shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id}.
- `target_type`
  > Type of entity being favorited (e.g., 'product', 'inquiry', 'address').
  > Defines the linked domain for the favorite record.
- `target_id`
  > ID of the entity being favorited, variable by type (product, inquiry,
  > address).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when favorite was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when favorite was last updated (modify, restore, remove).
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete indicator for favorite removal/reversal. Null if active.

### `shoppingmall_favorite_products`

Links each favorite record to a detailed product snapshot to preserve
product state as of favoriting. References shoppingmall_favorites and
shoppingmall_products. Used for accurate historical display, recovery,
and analytics on product changes versus time-of-favoriting.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `favorite_id`
  > Reference to the master favorite record's {@link
  > shoppingmall_favorites.id}.
- `product_id`: Favorited product's [shoppingmall_products.id](#shoppingmall_products).
- `product_snapshot_id`
  > Reference to the product's state at the time of favoriting ({@link
  > shoppingmall_product_snapshots.id}).
- `product_title`: Product title when favorited, for fast favorite browsing UI.
- `main_image_uri`: Main image URI as of favoriting for display in favorites list.
- `price_at_favorite`: Product price at time of favoriting for audit/restoration.
- `inventory_status`
  > Product inventory status (in_stock, out_of_stock, discontinued) at the
  > time of favoriting.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of favorite-product snapshot creation.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last update to product favorite (UI refresh, restoration,
  > etc.).

### `shoppingmall_favorite_inquiries`

Links each favorite record to a product/inquiry Q&A, preserving relevant
Q&A content, responder, and status as of favoriting. Supports evidence
tracking and recovery workflows.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `favorite_id`
  > Favorite record's [shoppingmall_favorites.id](#shoppingmall_favorites), unique per inquiry
  > per actor.
- `inquiry_id`: Referenced inquiry [shoppingmall_inquiries.id](#shoppingmall_inquiries).
- `inquiry_answer_id`
  > Linked answer for the inquiry at time of favoriting, if answered ({@link
  > shoppingmall_inquiry_answers.id}).
- `question`: Inquiry question text at time of favorite action.
- `answer`: Answer text, if available, at time of favorite action for snapshot/audit.
- `responder_actor_profile_id`: Actor profile ID for responder of answer, if answered when favorited.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of favorite-inquiry record creation.
- `updated_at`
  > Last update timestamp, such as after answer is posted or user triggers
  > refresh.

### `shoppingmall_favorite_addresses`

Links a favorite record to a user address, capturing address details and
preferences as of favoriting for autofill/recovery. Used for order flows
and analytics on favorite address use and engagement.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `favorite_id`: Reference to [shoppingmall_favorites.id](#shoppingmall_favorites).
- `actor_profile_id`
  > Owner profile for the favorite address, usually the same actor as the
  > favorite action. References [shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id](#shoppingmall_actor_profiles).
- `address_label`: Friendly label for display (e.g., 'Home', 'Office').
- `recipient_name`: Recipient's full name for shipping/delivery.
- `postal_address`: Full postal address as string for autofill purposes.
- `postcode`: Postal/ZIP code, validated per region.
- `phone_number`: Contact phone number for deliveries.
- `email`: Email for delivery/contact where captured.
- `is_default`: Flag indicating whether this is the default favorite address for the user.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of favorite-address snapshot creation.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for address (edit, restoration, etc.).

### `shoppingmall_favorite_snapshots`

Stores immutable snapshots of the full favorite record and its target
entity as of the favorite or recovery action. Enables policy-compliant
auditing, recovery within time windows, and advanced engagement
analytics. Provides a point-in-time export of favorite state.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `favorite_id`
  > Favorite record whose snapshot this represents. References {@link
  > shoppingmall_favorites.id}.
- `snapshot_type`: Action triggering this snapshot (created, restored, deleted, updated).
- `snapshot_data`
  > JSON-encoded or stringified business state of the favorite and its entity
  > at snapshot time.
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_favorite_events`

Tracks all business-relevant events tied to a favorite (add, remove,
restore, engagement, notification, failure). Used for event-driven
workflows, analytics, and error recovery. Enables full history and
auditing.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `favorite_id`: Related favorite's [shoppingmall_favorites.id](#shoppingmall_favorites).
- `event_type`: Type of event (created, removed, restored, notified, failed, etc.)
- `event_data`: Flexible JSON or data for more context about the event (if applicable).
- `actor_profile_id`: Actor profile responsible for the event.
- `created_at`: Timestamp the event occurred.

### `shoppingmall_favorite_notifications`

Stores notification events sent to users for favorite entities (price
drop, stock status, product change, restoration, etc.). References
favorite and recipient profile. Used for engagement tracking and
notification history/audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `favorite_id`
  > Favorite this notification relates to. References {@link
  > shoppingmall_favorites.id}.
- `recipient_actor_profile_id`
  > Recipient's profile for notification delivery; links to {@link
  > shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id}.
- `notification_type`: Business type of notification (price_drop, back_in_stock, removal, etc.).
- `notification_data`
  > JSON or detail about the notification sent (e.g., old/new prices for
  > price drop).
- `sent_at`: Timestamp notification sent.
- `read_at`: Timestamp when user read/acknowledged the notification, null if unread.

### `shoppingmall_favorite_restore_logs`

Stores detailed logs of favorite restoration actions (user-initiated or
admin-initiated), including evidence, actor profile, justification, and
timestamps. Enables robust auditing and compliance for recovery and legal
erasure requests. Links to favorite, snapshot, and actor profile.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `favorite_id`: Favorite being restored. References [shoppingmall_favorites.id](#shoppingmall_favorites).
- `actor_profile_id`
  > Actor profile (user or admin) who performed the restoration. References
  > [shoppingmall_actor_profiles.id](#shoppingmall_actor_profiles).
- `favorite_snapshot_id`
  > Snapshot used as basis for restoration ({@link
  > shoppingmall_favorite_snapshots.id}).
- `restore_reason`
  > Reason or context for restoration (user request, error reversal,
  > compliance).
- `evidence_data`
  > Auxiliary evidence or audit info (e.g., request object, attached files
  > list).
- `created_at`: Timestamp restore was performed.

### `shoppingmall_attachments`

Represents every unique attachment (file object) uploaded to the
platform. Tracks file-level identity and main business metadata. Core for
secure file management, permission, and audit. Linked to file metadata,
business objects (via links), and audit trails.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `originating_user_id`
  > ID of the user (customer, seller, or admin) who uploaded this attachment.
  > Used for access tracking and role enforcement.
- `uploaded_at`: Timestamp when the file was uploaded to the system (ISO 8601).
- `filename`: Name of the file as provided by uploader.
- `status`
  > Lifecycle status: e.g., active, archived, quarantined, deleted,
  > pending_moderation, rejected. Used for business workflows.
- `purpose`
  > Business context for file, e.g., 'product_image', 'order_receipt',
  > 'review_media', 'legal_evidence'.
- `file_type`
  > File type (MIME major/minor), e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf,
  > video/mp4, etc.
- `file_size`: File size in bytes.
- `checksum`: Cryptographic hash (e.g., SHA-256) for file integrity verification.
- `version_number`
  > Integer version for update/re-upload scenarios. Increments per
  > modification.
- `retention_policy`
  > Business or legal retention policy name/ID (e.g., 'default_5y',
  > 'invoice_7y', 'temp_30d').
- `deleted_at`: If soft deleted, when did this occur? Otherwise null.

### `shoppingmall_attachment_links`

Junction table linking attachments to business objects (products, orders,
reviews, inquiries) in the platform. Supports polymorphic associations
with strict referential integrity. Each entry represents a linkage from
one attachment to a target business entity. Enables querying all
attachments for any business object and vice versa.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `attachment_id`: Attachment referenced. [shoppingmall_attachments.id](#shoppingmall_attachments)
- `target_table`
  > Name of the table/entity this attachment is linked to. Polymorphic target
  > e.g., 'shoppingmall_products', 'shoppingmall_orders', etc.
- `target_id`: ID of the business object this attachment is linked to.
- `linked_by_user_id`
  > User who performed the link action (usually owner; could be admin for
  > compliance attachments).
- `linked_at`: Timestamp linkage created.

### `shoppingmall_file_metadata`

Stores detailed metadata for each file/attachment beyond core fields:
mime type, platform classification, retention, moderation flags,
automated scan results, and compliance status. Used for advanced audit,
compliance, and security scenarios.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `attachment_id`
  > Attachment for which this metadata record exists. {@link
  > shoppingmall_attachments.id}
- `metadata_json`
  > Structured business metadata (json). Includes detected labels, entities,
  > extracted text, moderation flags, etc.
- `virus_scan_status`
  > Result of last virus/malware scan: clean, flagged, quarantined,
  > scan_failed, etc.
- `scan_timestamp`: Last time a scan was performed.
- `compliance_status`
  > Business/legal compliance classification: compliant, flagged,
  > pending_review, legal_hold, expired, etc.
- `dmca_status`
  > DMCA/copyright status for file: normal, claimed, under_review, removed,
  > etc.
- `moderation_status`
  > Automated or human moderation status: clean, flagged, under_review,
  > blocked, etc.
- `last_updated_at`: Last update timestamp.

### `shoppingmall_attachment_audit`

Immutable audit log for all lifecycle changes to attachments. Captures
who, when, what action, and context for every mutation (upload, replace,
delete, quarantine, restore, legal hold, etc.). Used to ensure evidence
in compliance and legal investigations. Each entry is a permanent record.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `attachment_id`
  > Attachment affected by this audit event. {@link
  > shoppingmall_attachments.id}
- `actor_user_id`: User/admin who performed the action.
- `action_type`
  > Type of action: upload, delete, restore, quarantine, legal_hold, replace,
  > update_metadata, etc.
- `action_context`: JSON or human-readable context for the action (reason, details, IP, etc.).
- `created_at`: Immutable timestamp for when the audit entry was created.

### `shoppingmall_attachment_quarantine`

Tracks quarantine/judgment for attachments: files under threat, flagged
for abuse, under DMCA, or regulatory review. Used for pending assessment,
restriction, or forced removal. Describes the reason, business, and
technical context of the quarantine. Links to audit for traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `attachment_id`: Attachment under quarantine. [shoppingmall_attachments.id](#shoppingmall_attachments)
- `quarantine_reason`
  > Description or code explaining why the attachment was quarantined (virus,
  > DMCA, policy, abuse, etc.).
- `quarantined_by_user_id`: User/admin who flagged or quarantined the attachment.
- `quarantined_at`: When the file was quarantined.
- `status`: Current quarantine status: active, released, escalated, removed, etc.
- `release_context`
  > Details/context if/when quarantine was released (evidence, review notes,
  > etc.).

### `shoppingmall_attachment_appeals`

Records appeals lodged by users or sellers against attachment quarantine,
moderation, or removal actions. Supports the compliance
remediation/review process. Each record is a remediation request or
appeal and its resolution.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `attachment_id`
  > Attachment that is subject to the appeal process. {@link
  > shoppingmall_attachments.id}
- `appealing_user_id`: User (typically owner) initiating the appeal.
- `appeal_reason`: Business/message for the appeal. User-provided context.
- `appeal_timestamp`: Time when appeal was made.
- `resolution_status`: Status/outcome: pending, in_review, granted, denied, escalated, resolved.
- `resolution_user_id`: User/admin who resolved the appeal.
- `resolution_message`: Human/log note for outcome, including business/legal rationale.
- `resolution_timestamp`: Resolution time if resolved.

### `shoppingmall_attachment_retention`

Tracks active retention/expiry policies applied to each attachment for
compliance, legal, and business obligations. Maintains when a file
expires per rule, who configured policy, and critical event logs.
Guarantees files are managed as per contract, law, or internal policy.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `attachment_id`
  > The attachment file governed by this retention record. {@link
  > shoppingmall_attachments.id}
- `policy_id`
  > Policy code or name (e.g., invoice_7y, dmca_hold, default, temp_30d,
  > etc.).
- `policy_set_by_user_id`: Admin/user who set/changed this policy.
- `effective_from`: When retention policy starts for this attachment.
- `expires_at`: File scheduled expiration date/time per policy rules.
- `hold_status`
  > Whether file is on active hold preventing deletion: e.g., normal, hold,
  > legal_hold, extension, override.
- `created_at`: When this retention record was created.
- `updated_at`: Last updated time.

### `shoppingmall_attachment_incident_logs`

Records technical/business/security incidents involving attachments:
access violations, failed downloads, system errors, suspicious usage,
legal holds, or major administrative actions. Used for compliance
reporting, incident response, and platform monitoring.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `attachment_id`: Attachment involved in this incident. [shoppingmall_attachments.id](#shoppingmall_attachments)
- `incident_type`
  > Code or category, e.g., access_violation, download_fail, virus_detected,
  > orphan_cleanup, legal_hold_entry, etc.
- `incident_context`: Machine- or human-readable context data: JSON or detail string.
- `actor_user_id`: User or admin who triggered/logged the incident.
- `incident_timestamp`: When the incident was detected or logged.
- `resolution_status`: Outcome/status: open, closed, escalated, resolved, pending, etc.
- `resolution_message`: Message detailing the outcome, correction steps, or status for the record.
